terra.problem: The command to speak to the Israelites does not establish that everyone heard the message.
The introductions identifying Moses as Israel's leader and Aaron as a priest need references outside this passage.
Aaron's role as a priest is a fact from outside this passage and needs a reference.
The laundry requirements do not establish that the discharge is medically harmful.
Saying uncleanness goes onto the animal's back adds something the text does not say. It identifies the saddle as unclean.
The claim that nobody borrowed the man's saddle invents an action the text does not describe.
Saying sundown doesn't change a thing overlooks that the touched person is unclean until evening.
Saying the washing is 'the end of it' overlooks the instructions about the birds on the eighth day.
God speaks to Aaron as well as Moses in this passage.
Identifying Moses as Israel's leader is a fact from outside this passage and needs a reference.
The statement about what a grain offering consists of is a Bible fact from outside this passage and needs a reference.
The joke makes the length of the Bible verse part of the joke, rather than the human situation.
The verse does not say the person must stay put.
Saying her uncleanness lasts as long as the discharge does can imply it ends immediately with the discharge. Verse 28 says she counts seven days after being cleansed.
